skill.displayName: Leaf Curling & Margin Scorch Diagnosis | 植物卷叶/焦边识别（干旱/病害）

version.changelog:
- Major script refactor: main script renamed to `smyx_leaf_curling_scorch_diagnosis_analysis.py`, replacing old file.  
- Updated all documentation and SKILL.md to reference new script path and configuration file location.  
- Deprecated and removed legacy script and obsolete skill-card documentation files.  
- Applied multiple changes across 9 code and config files to support updated interfaces and naming.  
- Added missing main analysis script to the repository.  
- No changes to core diagnostic logic or operating procedures.

llm.summary: The skill’s plant diagnosis purpose is coherent, but it under-discloses account login or registration and local token storage tied to user identifiers.

dimensions.detail: Cloud-based image/video diagnosis and cloud history lookup fit the stated purpose, but the shared request helper can silently call a login/register endpoint using the supplied open-id, username, or phone number and then use the returned tokens for later API calls.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: The skill requires an open-id before diagnosis, reads it from local config when available, and asks for a username or phone number if missing; the instructions explain report saving/querying but do not clearly disclose automatic account creation/login or token caching.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No post-install or destructive installer behavior was found. The package has quality issues, including unresolved merge-conflict markers in SKILL.md and a likely invalid dependency entry, but these are not evidence of malware.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill uploads user-provided local files or forwards provided URLs to an external analysis service, which is expected for cloud diagnosis, but URL/file transfer and personal identifier transmission are not scoped with a clear consent or privacy boundary.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The common DAO creates a local SQLite database under the OpenClaw workspace data directory and stores user records plus access/open tokens; this persistence is not clearly described to users.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: Install only if you are comfortable sending plant images or videos, submitted URLs, and an open-id such as a username or phone number to the LifeEmergence/SMYX cloud service. Be aware that the skill may create or authenticate an account and store returned tokens locally in the OpenClaw workspace data directory; review and clear that data if you do not want persistent account state.
llm.findings:
[AST7] expected: The dynamic DAO filters are real but appear to be internal local database helpers, not exposed by the main diagnosis flow; this was not a basis for the Review verdict.
[SDI-2] unexpected: The scanner’s concern is supported in part: the artifact does more than simple diagnosis by using local config/user identifiers for authenticated cloud calls, with under-disclosed login/register and token behavior.
[SDI-4] unexpected: The open-id gating is inconsistent: the instructions say an open-id is mandatory, but also describe continuing after refusal; this weakens user control around authenticated operations.
[SQP-1] expected: Auto-triggering on plant leaf image analysis is broadly aligned with the skill purpose, but it becomes more sensitive because activation can lead to cloud upload and account-linked report handling.
[SQP-2] expected: External processing of plant media is expected for this cloud skill, but the artifacts insufficiently disclose file/URL transmission, personal identifier use, remote history access, and local credential persistence.
